sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Lake County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Four county offices share the job, and each answers a different question. The Lake County Treasurer sends out tax bills and collects the money; the phone is 847-377-2323. The Chief County Assessment Office oversees assessments, and the township assessors do the first-level work. The Board of Review hears assessment appeals. The County Clerk calculates the tax rates and handles redemption after a tax sale.

Lake County has 18 townships, and your township assessor is the first stop for a question about the value on your assessment notice. Your tax dollars mostly leave the county building: the county says Lake County government itself receives about seven percent of the average bill, while school districts get about 69 percent. More than 200 separate taxing bodies levy tax in the county.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lake County itself?
sections.html:
Lake County lies in the far northeast corner of Illinois, on the Wisconsin border and Lake Michigan, with Waukegan as seat and largest city. It spans 1,368 square miles including water, but only 444 of those are land. It is the only Illinois county with more water than land.

The Census Bureau counted 714,342 people in 2020 and estimates 719,339 for July 2025. Its 2020 to 2024 figures show a median home value of $345,700, owner-occupied housing at 74.8% and median household income of $110,416. The county issued 1,468 building permits in 2025. Households spend a median $2,503 a month on owner costs with a mortgage, which helps explain why a tax bill gets close attention.

The county lists dozens of cities and villages and many separate elementary and high school districts, so the mix of taxing bodies on a bill depends on the parcel. The district maps and the bill itself show which ones apply.

sections.h2: How does the Lake County property tax cycle work?
sections.html:
Each cycle takes two years, so the bill you pay reflects work done the year before. In year one, township assessors set values as of January 1 at one third of fair market value, using three years of sales. The county then equalizes values across townships, mails assessment notices known as blue sheets, and the Board of Review hears appeals. Taxing districts pass budgets and levies during the same year.

In year two, the Board finishes its hearings, the County Clerk figures tax rates from the levies and the final values, and the Treasurer mails bills at the start of May. The county's warning is blunt: by the time you get the bill, it is too late to protest it. The time to speak up is at the assessment notice and at the budget meetings of the taxing districts.

sections.h2: When are Lake County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in early May and are paid in two installments, in June and September. The calendar the Treasurer published for tax year 2025, payable in 2026, shows the pattern:

Lake County 2025 real estate tax calendar, payable in 2026 (source: Lake County Treasurer, Real Estate Tax Calendar)
DateEvent
May 1Property tax bills mailed
June 4First installment due
September 4Second installment due; last day to pay at local banks
October 2Last day to pay in the office to avoid publication and final notices
October 22Publication and final notice
November 12Last day to pay to avoid tax sale, by 5:00 p.m., no postmark
November 13Tax sale

The county says the due dates, interest dates and the tax sale date are fixed, while other dates on the calendar may shift for administrative reasons.

sections.h2: What does a late Lake County payment cost, and can you prepay?
sections.html:
State law requires the collector to add 1.5% per month to an unpaid installment, and the penalty is calculated on the 5th of each month and is not prorated. For the 2026 collection, a first installment paid between June 5 and July 4 carried 1.5%, and by the October 5 to November 12 window it reached 7.5%. The second installment started at 1.5% on September 5 and reached 3.0% in the last window.

  • Not receiving a bill, medical emergencies and travel do not qualify for forgiveness of the penalty
  • Forgiveness applies only to a documented Lake County error
  • In the final weeks before the sale, the Treasurer's Office takes only cash or certified funds, in person
  • A December prepayment window lets owners pay up to 50% of the previous year's bill, by check only, with the parcel number in the memo line

Homeowners with an escrow account should check the Treasurer's payment status page with the parcel number, since it can take weeks for a payment to show as paid.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Lake County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 30 calendar days from the date your township's assessments are published, so the deadline differs by township. The 2026 final filing dates ran from August 24 for Benton and Ela townships to November 2 for Shields. Waukegan's closed September 8, Libertyville's September 21 and Antioch's October 19, and all of those have passed.

The Board of Review wants owners to talk to the township assessor first, and requires it for factual-error appeals. Appeals are filed online through the Smartfile system. The county names these reasons as typical:

  • A factual error such as the wrong square footage
  • An assessment above one third of the recent sale price
  • An assessment above one third of market value
  • An assessment higher than comparable properties

You may choose a hearing by letter, phone, in person or Zoom, and corporations and LLCs must use an attorney. Hearings are finished in early February. Miss the window and the right to appeal that year's assessment is lost.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Lake County tax bill?
sections.html:
Exemptions are filed through the Smartfile e-filing portal run by the Chief County Assessment Office, and staff will help by phone or in person.

  • General homestead: lowers equalized assessed value by $8,000 for the owner's primary residence as of January 1, and does not need annual renewal
  • Senior exemption: another $8,000, which can be claimed on top of the general homestead
  • Senior assessment freeze: protects limited-income seniors from increases from rising values, but not from higher tax rates
  • Senior tax deferral: lets qualified seniors defer part or all of the tax on their residence
  • Home improvement, disabled persons and veterans exemptions

Exemptions do not transfer to a newly assigned parcel number, so a split or combined lot needs a fresh application under the new number.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Lake County taxes at the tax sale?
sections.html:
The Treasurer must sell unpaid taxes each year, and the sale is held in November, after final notices go out in October. The county says it does not sell the house, only the unpaid taxes. A buyer pays the taxes, the money goes to the taxing districts, and the owner then deals with the County Clerk's Office on redemption.

A seller who owes tax should settle the balance at or before closing. Ask the Treasurer for the current payoff, and ask the County Clerk for a redemption estimate if the parcel has already been sold. Payment status, prior-year delinquent taxes and a duplicate bill can all be requested from the Treasurer's Office.

faqs.q: When are Lake County, Illinois property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed in early May with two installments in June and September. For tax year 2025 they were due June 4 and September 4, 2026.

faqs.q: What is the Lake County penalty for late property tax?
faqs.a: The penalty is 1.5% per month on the unpaid installment, calculated on the 5th of each month and not prorated. The county forgives it only for a documented Lake County error.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Lake County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date your township's assessments are published. The 2026 windows ended between August 24 and November 2, depending on the township.

faqs.q: Does the Lake County tax sale sell my house?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer sells only the unpaid taxes. The owner then redeems through the Lake County Clerk's Office.

faqs.q: Can I prepay Lake County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in a December window set by the Treasurer. A prepayment is limited to 50% of the previous year's bill and must be paid by check with the parcel number in the memo.
